questions.question: What are the four recurring orchestration patterns in 2026 agent frameworks?
options: Sequential, Parallel, Conditional, Loop
Supervisor-worker, Swarm/peer-to-peer, Hierarchical, Debate
Plan-execute, Monitor-act, Sense-plan-act, Reactive
Chain, Tree, Graph, Star
questions.explanation: The four recurring orchestration patterns are: Supervisor-worker (central router dispatches to specialists), Swarm/peer-to-peer (direct handoffs, no central router), Hierarchical (supervisors managing sub-supervisors), and Debate (parallel proposers with cross-critique).

questions.question: What is the 2026 LangChain recommendation for implementing supervision?
options: Always use create_supervisor() for consistency
Do supervision through direct tool calls rather than create_supervisor(), for finer context engineering control
Use hierarchical rather than supervisor for any production system
Avoid supervision patterns entirely and use swarm instead
questions.explanation: LangChain's 2026 recommendation: do supervision through direct tool calls rather than the create_supervisor() library function. This gives finer context engineering control — you decide exactly what each specialist sees.

questions.question: What is Anthropic's guidance on when to add multi-agent topology?
options: Always start with multi-agent to avoid refactoring later
Add topology only when a single agent plus five workflow patterns is insufficient; success is about the right system for your needs
Use multi-agent for any task with more than 3 steps
Multi-agent is only needed for tasks that take more than an hour
questions.explanation: Anthropic: 'Success in the LLM space isn't about building the most sophisticated system. It's about building the right system for your needs.' Decision order: 1) single agent + workflow patterns, 2) supervisor-worker, 3) swarm, 4) hierarchical, 5) debate.

questions.question: What is the key advantage of swarm over supervisor topology, and its key disadvantage?
options: Advantage: easier to debug; disadvantage: more expensive
Advantage: lower latency (fewer routing hops); disadvantage: harder to reason about (no single point of control)
Advantage: more accurate; disadvantage: slower convergence
Advantage: cheaper; disadvantage: requires more specialized agents
questions.explanation: Swarm's advantage: lower latency because agents hand off directly without going through a central router. Disadvantage: harder to reason about and debug because there is no single point of control — hop counters are needed to prevent A->B->A bouncing.

questions.question: When should you use hierarchical topology?
options: For any system with more than 5 agents
Only when a single supervisor's context budget cannot hold descriptions of all specialists
When all agents need to communicate with all others
When you need the lowest possible latency
questions.explanation: Hierarchical (supervisors managing sub-supervisors) is appropriate only when a single supervisor cannot hold descriptions of all specialists within its context budget. Adding hierarchy for fewer agents creates complexity without benefit.

questions.question: What is the 'topology-first thinking' anti-pattern?
options: Spending too much time designing the topology before writing any code
Reaching for multi-agent before identifying what specific problem multi-agent actually solves
Choosing a topology based on familiarity rather than requirements
Implementing all four topologies and switching between them
questions.explanation: Topology-first thinking is the anti-pattern of deciding 'we need multi-agent' before identifying what problem multi-agent solves. Always start with single agent + workflow patterns and escalate only when those fall short.
